body.p: In the past, old people didn't die. They made their own kettles out of clay.[StN]: kalaÅ¡alawar - ACC.REFL?They made good kettles for themselves, they painted them. When a kettle broke, they cried. [StN]: on=how&when RUS calque? An old woman once had a daughter. The boys [lit.: men] were still children. Strangers from another family came to suggest her daughter for marriage. She did not want to give her daughter away. It was getting dark at night, they were still sitting. They heard crying in the yurt. When they came, [one of them] said: "Why are they crying? Is their kettle broken? They came to look â [one of them] said: "What happened? What, is the kettle broken? He said: "No! The kettle isn't broken![StN]: why ACC? Mother has died!" Diseases came to make a match. Then they began to die, they died.[StN]: ?
